summary: Andorra requires no visa of any kind and has no airport: it is reached through France or Spain, so Schengen rules decide who can come. EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities can travel there freely, while travelers who need a Schengen visa must hold a double- or multiple-entry one, because Andorra is outside the Schengen Area.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa.

passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must follow the Schengen passport rules, because you travel through France or Spain: your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before you arrive and be valid for at least 3 months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen Area.

source.name: UK FCDO — Andorra travel advice (entry requirements)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states whether travel insurance is required to enter Andorra. The EU Visa Code requires travellers who need a Schengen visa, the visa needed to reach Andorra through France or Spain, to hold travel medical insurance with minimum cover of EUR 30,000. The UK government says the EHIC and GHIC are not valid in Andorra and advises taking out comprehensive travel and medical insurance before travelling.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex

currencyLimits.text: Spain's tax agency says cash of EUR 10,000 or more must be declared when you enter or leave the EU, including on the way to or from Andorra. No Andorran official source we could find states Andorra's own threshold.

notes: Andorra is not in the EU. According to the UK FCDO, you may have to pay taxes and duties on tobacco, liquor and luxury goods when you re-enter France or Spain, and customs officers may impound excess tobacco and the vehicle carrying it.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says street crime is rare but to look after your belongings, that although Andorra has no recent history of terrorism, attacks cannot be ruled out, and that if you plan to ski you should check the weather and avalanche safety advice before you travel.

tips.text: If you needed a visa to enter the Schengen Area, the Government of Canada advises holding a multiple-entry visa before visiting Andorra: Andorra is outside Schengen, and holders of a single-entry visa may be refused re-entry to France or Spain.
Andorra is landlocked and has no airport, according to the Government of Canada; you must enter through France or Spain.

The UK FCDO says France and Spain have strict rules on the amount of tobacco exported from Andorra for personal use, and that customs officers may impound excess amounts of tobacco and the vehicle transporting it.
From 1 November to 15 May you must use winter tyres or carry snow chains in Andorra, and you can be fined if you do not (UK FCDO).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Andorra?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says the Principality does not require any type of visa. Entry is governed by Schengen rules because you must pass through France or Spain: EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities (US, UK, Japan and many more) need no visa, and if your passport needs a Schengen visa, the Andorran government says to get a double- or multiple-entry one so you can re-enter France or Spain afterward.

faq.question: Does time in Andorra count against my 90-day Schengen allowance?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says the Principality is not a member of the Schengen Area, and the Schengen 90-day limit counts stays on the territory of the Schengen states.

faq.question: Can I visit Andorra on a single-entry Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says travellers who need a Schengen visa must apply for a double- or multiple-entry one, and Canada's travel advice says holders of a single-entry visa will face delays and may be refused re-entry when returning to France or Spain.

faq.question: How do I get to Andorra without an airport?
faq.answer: By road, through France or Spain: Andorra has no airport (Government of Canada). From 1 November to 15 May, winter tyres or snow chains are compulsory on Andorran roads (UK FCDO).

faq.question: What currency does Andorra use?
faq.answer: The euro. According to the European Commission, Andorra is not in the euro area but has a monetary agreement with the EU that makes the euro its official currency.
